linux.fallback: configured access as written, not sshd's effective policy (Match is not evaluated); key comments, option values and key-file paths are never emitted; a home the agent cannot open is refused, not empty (constrained is the common unprivileged outcome); a symlinked key file or .ssh is refused; network mounts are skipped
linux.mechanism: bounded reads of /etc/ssh/sshd_config (Include followed, config symlinks followed as sshd does) and each account's authorized_keys (no-follow; pure parsers, SHA-256 fingerprints); one bounded systemctl is-enabled argv per sshd unit

macos.fallback: configured access as written, not sshd's effective policy; the launchd override is not 'running'; key comments, option values and key-file paths are never emitted; a symlinked key file or .ssh is refused; network mounts are skipped
macos.mechanism: bounded reads of /etc/ssh/sshd_config (Include followed, config symlinks followed as sshd does) and each account's authorized_keys (no-follow; pure parsers, SHA-256 fingerprints); one bounded launchctl print-disabled system argv

windows.fallback: not read yet: one unsupported status row, windows:planned

caveats: **Configured, not effective.** Rows report what the files say, not what `sshd` enforces: a `Match` block is counted and not evaluated, defaults are not applied (an unset setting is `-`), and an `Include` wildcard is expanded in byte order where `sshd` uses `glob(3)`'s locale order (it only matters when two included files set the same setting). Symlinks follow a two-tier rule. Under `/etc/ssh` (writable by root only: `sshd_config`, the Include directory, each Include file) a link is followed as `sshd` follows it, so stock macOS (`crypto.conf` links to `crypto/apple.conf`) and NixOS read as `SUPPORTED`; a link target outside `/etc/ssh` is read, with no owner or mode check on the target (`sshd` applies none to its config), and a non-regular target is still refused. A home parent (`/home`, `/Users`) is root-owned like `/etc/ssh`, so one link hop is allowed (Fedora Atomic ships `/home -> var/home`): the link is resolved by `readlink`, its target is checked against the mount table before anything is opened, and the target is then opened component by component with no further link followed (a link chain or a linked component is refused as `homes:eloop`); only the entries beneath it are the account's to write. Where the audited account can write (a home, `.ssh`, `authorized_keys*`, an absolute `AuthorizedKeysFile` path) a link is never followed, because a root agent would read what the account cannot: that file reports `failed` with a `symlink_refused`/`enotdir` token and the listing is `CONSTRAINED`. An absolute `AuthorizedKeysFile` path is opened from `/` one component at a time, so a link anywhere in its directory chain (stock macOS `/etc`, `/var` and `/tmp` are links to `/private/*`) is reported `failed` with `symlink_refused`, with no allow-list of platform aliases.

**A syntactic inventory, not `sshd`'s validity check.** A key row means the line parses by `sshd`'s grammar and its blob decodes completely. Option **values** are not validated (a nonsense `expiry-time` or `environment` still counts), an ECDSA point is checked for its length and `0x04` prefix but not for lying on the curve, a certificate's signature is not verified (its structure is), and a key of a type this plugin does not know (`ssh-dss`, a newer algorithm) is inventoried over its raw blob with the `unknown_type` flag and no size; a row flagged `unknown_type` records a line present in the file, not a key sshd is known to accept: OpenSSH 10 refuses an unknown type at parse time; whether this host's sshd knows the type is not checked. A tampered certificate or off-curve point that `sshd` would reject can therefore appear here. A certificate row reports the fingerprint of the embedded key, so a fingerprint is not an identifier of the certificate itself.

**Identity is the home directory's name.** `account` is the basename of the home directory the plugin walked (`/home/<name>`, `/root`, `/Users/<name>`, `/var/root`; macOS entries owned by a uid under 500 are skipped), not the login name, and accounts whose home is elsewhere (a directory-service or relocated home) are not walked. An `AuthorizedKeysFile` entry with `%u`, `%U` or another token needs the login name and is reported as unsupported rather than guessed. An account whose home the agent cannot open is `refused`, so a Linux listing from the unprivileged agent is usually `CONSTRAINED` (see Privileges).

**Blocking I/O on mounts is guarded by name.** Homes and key paths under a network filesystem named by the mount table (`yuzu::shared::is_network_fstype`, plus `webdav`/`afpfs`/`macfuse`/`osxfuse` on macOS; a home parent that is a link is checked at its target as well) are never opened, because an open on a dead hard mount pins a worker with no deadline. The list is by filesystem name, so a stacked filesystem or a bare `fuse` mount over a dead server still blocks (#4875), and a late mount after the run-start snapshot is not seen.

**Windows is planned, not read.** The Windows leg (per-profile `.ssh\authorized_keys`, `%ProgramData%\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys` and `sshd_config` via the profile walk, with the OpenSSH Server service state) reports one `unsupported` row, `windows:planned`; the Windows leg follows as its own PR. The effective policy (`sshd -T`, which evaluates `Match` and applies defaults) is not run on any OS; this plugin reports configured access only.

definitions.description: Who can log in over SSH, as configured: the sshd_config values that govern inbound access (read as written, Include followed, first occurrence wins; Match blocks are counted and not evaluated, defaults are not applied, so this is configured access and not sshd's effective policy), a SHA-256 fingerprint for every public key in each account's authorized_keys (a certificate reports the fingerprint of the key it carries) with the option names it uses, and whether the sshd service is enabled. Key comments, option values, principals and key-file paths are never emitted; the account is the home directory's name. A home or file the agent cannot read is reported as refused with a reason token (on Linux an unprivileged agent usually cannot open other users' homes, so constrained is the common outcome), never as an empty result. A key row flagged unknown_type records a line present in the file, not a key sshd is known to accept: OpenSSH 10 refuses an unknown type at parse time; whether this host's sshd knows the type is not checked. Reads one machine per request and is off until enabled. The Windows leg is planned and not yet read. A leading status row states whether the read was complete.

description: SSH inbound-access audit: sshd_config as written, per-account authorized_keys fingerprints, sshd service state; never key comments, option values or paths
how_it_works:
`list` reports who can log in to this host over SSH, as configured, in four parts: the `sshd_config` values that govern inbound access, the public keys each account trusts, whether the `sshd` service is enabled, and where each fact came from. It changes nothing. The first row is always a `status` row saying whether the read was complete, then three `source` rows (`sshd_config`, `homes`, `service`; each says `read`, `absent`, `refused` or `failed`, so zero `key` rows is never an ambiguous empty success), then a `config` row for every allowlisted setting, the `service` rows, and finally one `file` row per `authorized_keys` file followed by one `key` row for every key line `sshd` would accept.

`sshd_config` is read as `sshd` reads it: the first value of a setting wins in directive order, `Include` files are parsed at the directive's position (relative paths are taken under `/etc/ssh/`, a leaf wildcard is expanded in byte order, up to 4 levels and 32 files), and a `Match` block is counted but never evaluated and nothing inside it is applied. `AuthorizedKeysFile` decides which files are read per account (`.ssh/authorized_keys` and `.ssh/authorized_keys2` when unset; `%h` and `%%` are expanded, `%u`, `%U` and `~` are reported as unsupported rather than guessed). A key row carries the type, the fingerprint (`SHA256:` plus unpadded base64, byte-identical to `ssh-keygen -lf`; a certificate reports the key it carries), the key size, flags (`certificate`, `cert_authority`, `has_command`, `has_from`, `has_principals`, `unknown_type`) and the option **names** it uses. Every key blob and certificate is decoded completely and within bounds, and trailing bytes are refused. A key comment, an option **value** (`command=`, `from=`, `principals=`), a principals list and any key-file path are never emitted, not even in the `authorizedkeysfile` config row, which says only `default`, `none` or `custom:<n>`.
name: remote_access_audit

columns.description: Row shape discriminator (field 0). Values: status, source, config, service, file, key.
columns.name: row_kind

columns.description: status: the literal "list". source: sshd_config, homes or service. config: the setting (permitrootlogin, passwordauthentication, pubkeyauthentication, kbdinteractiveauthentication, permitemptypasswords, usepam, port, authorizedkeysfile, allowusers_count, allowgroups_count, denyusers_count, denygroups_count, match_blocks). service: the unit (ssh.service, sshd.service, ssh.socket, or com.openssh.sshd on macOS). file and key: the account, which is the HOME DIRECTORY NAME, not necessarily the login name.
columns.name: field_1

columns.description: status: supported, constrained, permission_denied or unsupported (the planned Windows leg, and a leg that threw). source: read, absent, refused or failed (absent is a state, not a failure). config: the value as written in the first occurrence, "-" when unset or sshd_config was not read; authorizedkeysfile reports only default, none or custom:<n>, never a path; the counts are numbers. service: the state - systemctl is-enabled output (enabled, enabled-runtime, linked, linked-runtime, alias, masked, masked-runtime, static, indirect, disabled, generated, transient, bad, not-found) or enabled/disabled for launchd, or unknown (never read as disabled). file: authorized_keys, authorized_keys2 or custom. key: the same kind.
columns.name: field_2

columns.description: status: reason token(s) for a non-supported read, "-" when complete; tokens look like linux:remote_access_audit:homes:permission_denied or windows:planned. source: files read (sshd_config plus includes), accounts walked, or units queried, "-" unless read. config: where the value came from (sshd_config or include:<file name>), "-" when unset. service: the mechanism. file: read, absent, refused or failed. key: the key type as written (ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa, ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, a -cert-v01 certificate type, ...).
columns.name: field_3

columns.description: file: the number of key lines accepted, "-" unless read. key: the fingerprint, SHA256: plus unpadded base64, identical to ssh-keygen -lf (a certificate reports the key it carries).
columns.name: field_4

columns.description: file: the number of lines sshd would not accept (unparseable key, unknown option, truncated or trailing-byte blob, RSA under 1024 bits), "-" unless read. key: the key size in bits (RSA modulus, 256 for ed25519, the curve size for ECDSA), "-" for a key of an unknown type.
columns.name: field_5

columns.description: file: the number of lines over 16 KiB that were not parsed, "-" unless read. key: comma-separated flags from cert_authority, certificate, has_command, has_from, has_principals, unknown_type, or "-". A row flagged unknown_type records a line present in the file, not a key sshd is known to accept: OpenSSH 10 refuses an unknown type at parse time; whether this host's sshd knows the type is not checked.
columns.name: field_6

columns.description: key: the lowercased option NAMES the line carries (restrict, cert-authority, [no-]port-forwarding, [no-]agent-forwarding, [no-]x11-forwarding, [no-]touch-required, [no-]verify-required, [no-]pty, [no-]user-rc, command, principals, from, expiry-time, environment, permitopen, permitlisten, tunnel), or "-". Option VALUES are never emitted. Not used by the other kinds.
columns.name: field_7

outputs_note: Every row is pipe-delimited; field 0 is the row kind, `-` is an absent value, and the first row is always `status|list|<supported\|constrained\|permission_denied\|unsupported>|<reason or ->`. The rest, in this order: `source|<sshd_config\|homes\|service>|<read\|absent\|refused\|failed>|<count or ->` (files read including includes, accounts walked, units queried); `config|<key>|<value or ->|<sshd_config\|include:<file> or ->` for each of `permitrootlogin`, `passwordauthentication`, `pubkeyauthentication`, `kbdinteractiveauthentication` (the deprecated `ChallengeResponseAuthentication` shares its slot), `permitemptypasswords`, `usepam`, `port` (comma-joined across occurrences), `authorizedkeysfile` (`default\|none\|custom:<n>`), `allowusers_count`, `allowgroups_count`, `denyusers_count`, `denygroups_count` and `match_blocks` (always all thirteen; `-` when `sshd_config` was not read, and an unset setting is `-` because defaults are not applied); `service|<unit>|<state>|<mechanism>` (the `systemctl is-enabled` words `enabled`, `enabled-runtime`, `linked`, `linked-runtime`, `alias`, `masked`, `masked-runtime`, `static`, `indirect`, `disabled`, `generated`, `transient`, `bad`, `not-found`, or `unknown`; on macOS `com.openssh.sshd` is `enabled`, `disabled` or `unknown`, and `enabled` is a launchd override, not "running"); `file|<account>|<authorized_keys\|authorized_keys2\|custom>|<read\|absent\|refused\|failed>|<keys>|<malformed>|<oversized>`; and `key|<account>|<kind>|<type>|<fingerprint>|<bits or ->|<flags or ->|<option names or ->`. The account is the home directory's name, not necessarily the login name. A `key` row flagged `unknown_type` records a line present in the file, not a key sshd is known to accept: OpenSSH 10 refuses an unknown type at parse time; whether this host's sshd knows the type is not checked. Every free field is scrubbed of NUL and invalid UTF-8, pipe-escaped and cut at 4096 bytes.

privileges.grant: None for `launchctl print-disabled system`, which answers an unprivileged caller. Reading another user's `~/.ssh` needs the access the agent identity already has as root; an identity that cannot open a home reports it refused
privileges.if_refused: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / partial with `macos:remote_access_audit:<source>:permission_denied` when a source was refused and none was read, `CONSTRAINED` when another source was read; the `file` row says `refused`
privileges.measured: `launchctl print-disabled system` and `/etc/ssh` reads verified as a normal user on macOS 26.6.2; see Sample output

privileges.grant: None for `sshd_config` and `systemctl is-enabled` (world-readable and unprivileged). **Other users' homes are usually 0700 or 0750, so an unprivileged agent cannot open them: `CONSTRAINED` with `linux:remote_access_audit:homes:permission_denied` and one `refused` file row per account is the common outcome, never "no keys".** The real options are `CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH` on the agent binary or accepting the refusal; do not loosen home modes
privileges.if_refused: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / partial with `linux:remote_access_audit:<source>:permission_denied` when a source was refused and none was read, `CONSTRAINED` when another source was read
privileges.measured: Not measured on the `yuzu` account; the capture runs as euid 0 in a container, see Sample output
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon, dedicated unprivileged account (`yuzu`), never root by design (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

result_status.when: every source that exists was read in full; no keys is `supported` with `file` rows saying `absent` or `read|0`

result_status.provenance: `<os>:remote_access_audit:sshd_config:<cause>`, `<os>:remote_access_audit:include:<cause>`, `<os>:remote_access_audit:keys:<cause>`, with `<cause>` one of `symlink_refused`, `not_regular`, `oversized`, `invalid_bytes`, or an errno token (`eio`, `eloop`, `enotdir`, `enametoolong`, `errno_<n>`)
result_status.when: a file could not be read: a symlinked key-side file, `.ssh` or home (refused, never followed), a config link that dangles (`include:enoent`, as `sshd` refuses to start) or loops (`include:eloop`), a FIFO or other non-regular target, a file over 256 KiB (config) or 1 MiB (keys), a NUL byte in `sshd_config` or an `Include` file (in `authorized_keys` a NUL cuts that line only, see the keys row below), an I/O error; its source or `file` row says `failed` and the other sources are still reported
a configuration line has an unterminated quote and was skipped, as `sshd` would refuse it
an `Include` was not followed: nested deeper than 4 levels, more than 32 files in all, inside a `Match` block (whose condition is not evaluated), or a `~` path or wildcard in a directory component
an `AuthorizedKeysFile` entry uses `%u`, `%U`, another token or `~` and was skipped (never guessed), or `AuthorizedKeysFile` also appears inside a `Match` block (the global value is used)

an `authorized_keys` line `sshd` would not accept (unparseable key, unknown option, a second `command`/`from`/`principals`, truncated or trailing-byte blob, RSA under 1024 bits) or a line over 16 KiB was counted and not emitted; or a key of a type this plugin does not know was inventoried over its raw blob; or a line held a NUL byte and was read only up to it, as `sshd` reads it (the file row stays `read` and the key before the NUL is reported)

a home root, home or key path on a network filesystem named by the run-start mount table was never opened; or the mount table could not be read (the walk proceeds unguarded); or more than 512 accounts, 1024 key-file reads or 2048 rows / 1 MiB were reached (the listing stops there); or a field was cut at 4096 bytes

the service query failed: the tool is not installed (a non-systemd host, which is a failed service source and never "disabled"), timed out, was cut short, printed nothing or something unrecognised; the `service` source row says `failed`
a source was refused and no source was read; accumulated constrained tokens may follow, comma-joined
the bounded runner could not start the tool (reported through the service query, which then constrains the listing)
a leg threw: an `unsupported` status row, reported instead of unwinding across the plugin boundary

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore, queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`. `list` is also a gathered definition (`crossplatform.security.remote_access_audit`, 3600s TTL).
**Not consumed by** daily-sync, TAR, DEX, or metrics.

**Default off, and how to turn it on.** The plugin is Forensics-class and ships off: the server seeds a default-off kill switch at boot, so nothing dispatches until an operator runs `PUT /api/v1/plugin-config/remote_access_audit/kill-switch {"enabled":true}`. After that, dispatch is gated at `Forensics:Read` with `AdminOrApproval` (Administrator by default) and is single-target: exactly one device per request.

**Sensitivity.** Per-account key fingerprints on one named machine are identity material: they say which keys can log in as which account, and the account is the home directory's name. Key comments, option values, principals lists and key-file paths are never emitted. The stored result is readable by `Response:Read` holders, as for every plugin (known gap #4990), and the Instructions UAT runner cannot exercise Forensics-tier dispatch (known gap #5261); neither is fixed here.
**Siblings:** `privacy_permissions`, `browser_inventory` and `execution_artifacts` (the other Forensics-class plugins) and `mgmt_posture` (which plane controls the device).
